title: "Contributing"
subtitle: "What is welcome now, and what is not yet"

::: {.callout-warning}
## Honest expectations first

Recueil is written by one person to replace a stack they use daily.
[ADR-0014](https://github.com/etabli-dev/etabli-recueil/blob/main/spec/adr/0014-tool-for-you-through-m3-open-repo-at-m4.md)
sets when that changes: the repository is public and AGPL from the first commit, but the project is
developed as a tool for its author through **M3** (the end of Phase 3) and opens properly at **M4**
(the end of Phase 5). Until then:

- no support commitment and no roadmap promise;
- issues and pull requests may sit for a long time, or be closed with a short reason;
- the plugin API may break between minor versions, and the data model may change under a migration;
- a large unsolicited pull request is likely to be declined however good it is, because reviewing
  and then maintaining it costs more than the feature is worth at this stage.

None of that is meant to keep anyone out. **Bug reports, reproductions, corrections to the
specification and small focused patches are genuinely welcome now.** For anything larger, open an
issue and ask whether it fits — a five-minute answer beats a week of work being declined.
:::

This page is a summary. The authoritative document is
[`CONTRIBUTING.md`](https://github.com/etabli-dev/etabli-recueil/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) in the
repository, and it wins wherever the two differ.

## Ground rules

- Everyone taking part is covered by the
  [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/etabli-dev/etabli-recueil/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md).
- **Security problems do not go through the issue tracker.** See
  [SECURITY.md](https://github.com/etabli-dev/etabli-recueil/blob/main/SECURITY.md).
- **Prose is British English**, matching CONCEPT.md and the ADRs — comments, documentation and
  user-visible strings alike. Code identifiers follow their own ecosystem: npm's `package.json`
  keeps `license`, while the plugin manifest's own key is `licence`.
- **No AI attribution, anywhere.** No co-author trailer for a tool, no "generated with" line, no
  assistant signature in a commit message, a comment, a file header or a pull request description.
  Tools are tools; the person who submits a change is its author and is accountable for it. Pull
  requests carrying such lines will be asked to rewrite their history.

## Getting set up

| Tool | Version | Note |
|---|---|---|
| Node.js | 22 LTS or newer | 22 is what CI targets and what the image runs |
| pnpm | 9.x | `corepack enable && corepack prepare pnpm@9 --activate` |
| Git | any recent version | commits must be signed off |
| Docker | optional | only for the sidecar profiles and for building the image |

No database server is needed. v1 is SQLite only, and the file is created on first run.

```sh
pnpm install          # install the workspace
pnpm build            # build every package and app
pnpm test             # unit and integration tests (Vitest)
pnpm lint             # lint and format check
pnpm dev              # server and web UI in watch mode
```

::: {.callout-important appearance="simple"}
`pnpm build` and `pnpm test` are real and pass across the whole workspace. `pnpm lint` and `pnpm dev`
are declared at the root but not implemented in every package yet, so they are no-ops where a
package has no such script. The test suite needs **no container**: everything a sidecar would provide
— OCR, GROBID, a Paperless-ngx server, WebDAV, S3, IMAP — is behind an interface with an in-process
fake, and a test that required a container would be a test nobody runs.
:::

## Where the specification lives

Recueil is specified before it is written, and the specification is in the repository rather than a
wiki.

| File | What it settles |
|---|---|
| [`CONCEPT.md`](https://github.com/etabli-dev/etabli-recueil/blob/main/CONCEPT.md) | the whole thing: goals, non-goals, principles, architecture, roadmap. Start here |
| [`spec/data-model.md`](https://github.com/etabli-dev/etabli-recueil/blob/main/spec/data-model.md), [`spec/erd.mmd`](https://github.com/etabli-dev/etabli-recueil/blob/main/spec/erd.mmd) | entities, fields, relations |
| `spec/openapi.yaml` | the API contract |
| [`spec/hooks.md`](https://github.com/etabli-dev/etabli-recueil/blob/main/spec/hooks.md) | the v1 hook catalogue and its guarantees |
| [`spec/plugin-manifest.schema.json`](https://github.com/etabli-dev/etabli-recueil/blob/main/spec/plugin-manifest.schema.json) | `recueil.plugin.json`, validated at install and activation |
| [`spec/adr/`](https://github.com/etabli-dev/etabli-recueil/blob/main/spec/adr/) | every architectural decision |
| `docs/` | this site |

If a change contradicts something in `spec/`, either the change is wrong or the spec needs an ADR.
Say which in the pull request. See [decision records](adr.qmd) for when one is required and how to
write it.

## Commits

- **Subject:** imperative mood, under 72 characters, capitalised, no trailing full stop. "Add ISBN
  resolver", not "Added ISBN resolver".
- **Body:** wrapped at 72 characters, explaining **why**. The diff already says what. Note the
  alternatives you rejected.
- **Scope:** one logical change per commit. Move-only and rename-only changes go in their own commit
  so the substantive diff stays readable.
- **References:** `Refs #123`, `Closes #123` or `Implements ADR-0016` in the body, not the subject.

## Developer Certificate of Origin

Recueil uses the [DCO 1.1](https://developercertificate.org/) rather than a contributor licence
agreement. Nothing to sign, no copyright assigned: you keep yours, and your contribution is licensed
AGPL-3.0-or-later like the rest of the repository.

```sh
git commit -s -m "Add ISBN resolver"
```

Use a real name — a pseudonym you are known by is acceptable, an anonymous handle is not — and an
address that reaches you.

## Pull requests

1. Open an issue first for anything not small and obvious, and wait for a reply.
2. Branch from `main`. One topic per pull request.
3. Fill in the template: what and why, the linked issue, the roadmap phase, the checklist.
4. Keep the diff focused. Unrelated formatting churn is the usual reason a patch stalls.
5. Tests come with the change. Anything touching a public contract updates `spec/` in the same pull
   request.
6. Documentation comes with the change too, when there is user-visible behaviour to describe.
7. Expect review comments on British English, on ADR compliance, and on whether the change belongs
   to the phase it claims.

## Contributing to this site

The documentation is a Quarto website in `docs/`, published to GitHub Pages.

```sh
quarto preview docs     # live preview
quarto render docs      # build into docs/_site
```

Every page carries an edit link in its margin. `_site/` and `.quarto/` are generated and are not
committed.

Documentation-only changes need no ADR and no issue first. If a page describes behaviour that does
not exist, it must say so and name the phase that brings it — an unmarked promise in a manual is a
bug in the manual.

## Proposing a plugin

Most extensions should not be plugins at all; see [the plugins page](plugins.qmd) for the order of
preference and the hook catalogue. If it really is a plugin, read
[`spec/hooks.md`](https://github.com/etabli-dev/etabli-recueil/blob/main/spec/hooks.md) first: if
what you need is not in the v1 catalogue, your proposal is a request for a new hook, and new hooks
are contract changes that need an ADR.
